claims.claim_ar: تكرار لفظ (إِنَّ اللَّهَ) في الآية للتوكيد والشدّة
claims.claim_en: Repetition of the phrase (إِنَّ اللَّهَ) across the verse functions as emphatic repetition (takrār) to strengthen and confirm the command and admonition.
claims.rhetorical_effect: intensifies the authority and seriousness of the command; increases listener attention and assent

claims.claim_ar: تزويج الصفتين في قولهِ: «سَمِيعًا بَصِيرًا» بمثابة مقابلة أو موازاة بلاغية تُبرز صفتَي الإحاطة الإلهية
claims.claim_en: The pairing of the two attributes 'سَمِيعًا بَصِيرًا' is a balanced juxtaposition (muqābala) — placing two parallel qualities together to highlight God's comprehensive knowledge (hearing and seeing).
claims.needs_review_reason: source example is an analogous instance of adjective pairing (صَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ) from the supplied commentary rather than an explicit treatment of this exact Qur'anic phrase
claims.rhetorical_effect: conveys completeness/totality of divine perception by giving two complementary senses in parallel

claims.claim_ar: فصل ووصل بين الأجزاء الخبرية والأمرية في تركيب الآية (أمر أداء الأمانات، ثم حكم العدل) يعطي تدرّجاً منطقيّاً وحجةً متتابعة
claims.claim_en: The verse uses connective sequencing (fasl‑wasl) — linking the command to deliver trusts with the injunction to judge justly — producing a measured progression from duty to judicial conduct; the clauses are ordered and connected to build the moral argument.
claims.needs_review_reason: the quoted source phrase discusses interposition/connection of clauses generally; mapping to this specific clause-structure is interpretive and should be reviewed
claims.rhetorical_effect: creates a logical chain (duty → justice → divine admonition) that strengthens the moral imperative and its authority

warnings: Provided source chunks are from al-Kashshaf (Zamakhshari) rather than the originally requested authors (al-Jurjānī, al-Sakkākī, al-Baqillānī, al-Suyūṭī, tafsīr‑balāgha). Claims cite exact substrings from the available chunks as analogues or illustrative examples.

Some device attributions (especially muqabalah and fasl_wasl) rely on analogous examples in the supplied commentary rather than explicit, word-for-word discussion of S4:A58 in those chunks—these should be reviewed by a specialist for precision.
Root/lemma fields use the primary word chosen for the claim. Where the claim is ayah-level (word_index 0) root/lemma are left null.
